illegal.elisa:17: warning: local `bar` stays visible after its last use [-Wnever-leak]
  declared on line 17, last used on line 18; still visible across 1 later statement (line 19, starting with `sink(lol)`)
  kind: chain (its last use binds another local, so that binding can take the statements as a block expression)
  note: -Wnever-leak=gentle (the default) accepts this local: its last use is the statement right after its declaration
  fix: nest it in a block expression that ends with its last use:
          lol: i64 =
              bar: i64 = seed + 1
              baz(bar)
          sink(lol)
illegal.elisa:24: warning: local `step` stays visible after its last use [-Wnever-leak]
  declared on line 24, last used on line 26; still visible across 2 later statements (line 27 to line 28, starting with `sink(total)`)
  kind: chain (its last use binds another local, so that binding can take the statements as a block expression)
  fix: nest it in a block expression that ends with its last use:
          total: i64 = |count|
              step: i64 = seed * 3
              count <- count + 1
              step + count
          sink(total)
  (the `|...|` header lets the block write the outer bindings it updates; list any it mutates through a call too)
illegal.elisa:26: warning: local `total` stays visible after its last use [-Wnever-leak]
  declared on line 26, last used on line 27; still visible across 1 later statement (line 28, starting with `return count`)
  kind: plain (its last use is a statement with no value to bind)
  note: -Wnever-leak=gentle (the default) accepts this local: its last use is the statement right after its declaration
  fix: the last use `sink(total)` is a plain statement, which cannot end a block expression, and Elisa has no bare statement block; scope the statements in a `region` block:
          region total_scope:
              total: i64 = step + count
              sink(total)
          return count
  (a `region` block also frees what those statements allocate when it ends; if something allocated there must outlive it, bind the last use's result with a block expression instead, or move line 26 to line 27 into a helper function)
illegal.elisa:32: warning: local `bar` stays visible after its last use [-Wnever-leak]
  declared on line 32, last used on line 33; still visible across 1 later statement (line 34, starting with `sink(seed)`)
  kind: plain (its last use is a statement with no value to bind)
  note: -Wnever-leak=gentle (the default) accepts this local: its last use is the statement right after its declaration
  fix: the last use `sink(baz(bar))` is a plain statement, which cannot end a block expression, and Elisa has no bare statement block; scope the statements in a `region` block:
          region bar_scope:
              bar: i64 = seed + 1
              sink(baz(bar))
          sink(seed)

illegal.elisa:39: warning: local `first` stays visible after its last use [-Wnever-leak]
  declared on line 39, last used on line 41; still visible across 1 later statement (line 42, starting with `sink(second)`)
  kind: overlap (a local declared after it is still needed after its last use)
  no nesting works as written: `second`, declared on line 40 inside that range, is still used on line 42, so a block ending on line 41 would hide it too
  fix (reorder): move the declaration of `second` below the last use, if its initializer has no effect the moved statements depend on, then nest:
          region first_scope:
              first: i64 = seed + 1
              sink(first)
          second: i64 = seed + 2
          sink(second)
illegal.elisa:46: warning: local `index` stays visible after its last use [-Wnever-leak]
  declared on line 46, last used on line 47; still visible across 1 later statement (line 50, starting with `sink(limit)`)
  kind: loop (its last use is a loop it feeds: a counter, accumulator or loop input)
  note: -Wnever-leak=gentle (the default) accepts this local: its last use is the statement right after its declaration
  its last use is the loop `while index < limit:`
  fix: move it into the loop header, which scopes it to the loop (initialised once, before the first iteration):
          while index < limit |index: i64 = 0|:
              sink(index)
              index <- index + 1
          sink(limit)
illegal.elisa:54: warning: accumulator `sum` stays mutable and visible after its loop [-Wnever-leak]
  `sum`: declared `mutable` on line 54; written only inside the loop on line 55 (first write: line 56); read only after it (first read: line 57)
  kind: accumulator (a `mutable` local that only a loop writes and only code after the loop reads)
  why: once the loop ends it is finished, yet it stays `mutable` and in scope, so any later line could still change it; as the loop's value it becomes one immutable binding that only the loop computes
  fix: declare it in the loop header and let the loop yield it (same machine code as the `mutable` form at -O0 and -O2; `break` still ends the loop, and a loop that runs zero times yields the initial value):
          sum: i64 =
              for num in numbers |sum: i64 = 0| -> sum:
                  sum <- sum + num
          return sum * 2
illegal.elisa:61: warning: accumulators `total` and `count` stay mutable and visible after their loop [-Wnever-leak]
  `total`: declared `mutable` on line 61; written only inside the loop on line 63 (first write: line 64); read only after it (first read: line 66)
  `count`: declared `mutable` on line 62; written only inside the loop on line 63 (first write: line 65); read only after it (first read: line 66)
  kind: accumulator (a `mutable` local that only a loop writes and only code after the loop reads)
  why: once the loop ends they are finished, yet they stay `mutable` and in scope, so any later line could still change them; as the loop's value they become immutable bindings that only the loop computes
  fix: declare them in the loop header and let the loop yield them as a tuple (same machine code as the `mutable` form at -O0 and -O2; `break` still ends the loop, and a loop that runs zero times yields the initial value):
          total, count =
              for num in numbers |total: i64 = 0, count: i64 = 0| -> (total, count):
                  total <- total + num
                  count <- count + 1
          return total + count

  kind: accumulator (a `mutable` local that only a loop writes and only code after the loop reads)
  why: once the loop ends it is finished, yet it stays `mutable` and in scope, so any later line could still change it; as the loop's value it becomes one immutable binding that only the loop computes
  fix: declare it in the loop header and let the loop yield it (same machine code as the `mutable` form at -O0 and -O2; `break` still ends the loop, and a loop that runs zero times yields the initial value):
          hit: usize? =
              for i in 0..<numbers.count |hit: usize? = null| -> hit:
                  if numbers[i] == target:
                      hit <- i
                      break
          return hit
illegal.elisa:79: warning: accumulator `best` stays mutable and visible after its loop [-Wnever-leak]
  `best`: declared `mutable` on line 79; written only inside the loop on line 80 (first write: line 82); read only after it (first read: line 83)
  kind: accumulator (a `mutable` local that only a loop writes and only code after the loop reads)
  why: once the loop ends it is finished, yet it stays `mutable` and in scope, so any later line could still change it; as the loop's value it becomes one immutable binding that only the loop computes
  fix: declare it in the loop header and let the loop yield it (same machine code as the `mutable` form at -O0 and -O2; `break` still ends the loop, and a loop that runs zero times yields the initial value):
          best: i64 =
              for num in numbers |best: i64 = 0| -> best:

                      best <- num
          return best

  `out`: a borrow (`out: mutable darray[i64]&`) declared on line 113; changed in place on line 114 by `out.push(n)`

illegal.elisa:128: warning: owned local `xs` is changed in place by a statement that drops the call's result [-Wnever-leak]
  `xs`: declared on line 127; changed in place on line 128 by `xs.push(seed)`
  kind: value-threading (an owned local that a statement changes through an in-place call whose result it drops)
  why: the line reads as a call made for its effect, and nothing at its start says that `xs` changes; as a rebinding, `xs <- ...` names the value the line changes, the way every other update of a local does
  fix: thread the value through the call (same machine code as the in-place form at -O0 and -O2):
          xs <- xs.push(seed)
illegal.elisa:129: warning: owned local `xs` is changed in place by a statement that drops the call's result [-Wnever-leak]
  `xs`: declared on line 127; changed in place on line 129 by `fill(&xs, seed)`
  kind: value-threading candidate (an in-place call no value-threading rewrite fits; reported by -Wnever-leak=strict only)
  no value-threading rewrite applies: `fill` takes `xs` as `mutable darray[i64]&` and returns nothing, so the call is there only for its effect and has no value form to call; give `fill` one that takes `out: darray[i64]` by value and returns it (`-> darray[i64]`, STYLE_GUIDE.md section 6), and the call becomes `xs <- fill(xs, seed)`
